segments.text: here today because everyone deserves a safe, comfortable, affordable place to live. And without this, nothing in your life works. It's a place that you can make your own and take pride in. A home gives you the freedom and the opportunity to build the life that you want.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_221
segments.text: But for many Americans this dream is out of reach. In more than 90% of U.S. counties minimum wage workers can't afford even a modest one-bedroom apartment. Every

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_221
segments.text: day, Americans are trying to figure out how to afford their lives. And millions of our friends and neighbors have a hard time finding and affording a place to rent, let alone putting the money together for a down payment to buy a home of their own. So how did we get here? Well,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_224
segments.text: for decades, the United States has not invested enough in housing, in building housing. We have severely neglected public housing, and we have outsourced much of housing development to the private market.
And

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_221
segments.text: because of restrictive local zoning laws and rising construction costs, we haven't built nearly enough. Housing supply collapsed in the 2008 foreclosure crisis, and private equity firms and other big corporate interests moved in, and they were focused on delivering returns for their investors, not on solving the housing shortage. In Minneapolis and around the country, in Minnesota and around the country, investors with deep pockets started snatching up starter homes with all cash offers.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_221
segments.text: And families are being outbid by mysterious buyers thousands of miles away. Big corporate landlords, they're raising rents and they're ignoring tenant calls to fix the leaks and take care of the pests. And
our

segments.text: lays out a new way to meet people's needs through social housing.
